claim_boundary: Several pre-2019 Bitcoin studies report a positive Monday return effect, but a seven-exchange high-frequency study reports that return patterns were not persistent across time. This conflict justifies one exact post-literature replication, not a calendar-alpha claim and not a search over weekdays.

primary_sources.title: Bitcoin and the day-of-the-week effect
primary_sources.finding: Using 2010-2017 daily data, the study reports higher Monday returns and volatility relative to other weekdays.

primary_sources.title: The day of the week effect in the cryptocurrency market
primary_sources.finding: Bitcoin was the exception with significantly higher Monday returns, while the paper states that most simulated profit results were not significantly different from random outcomes.

primary_sources.title: Bitcoin time-of-day, day-of-week and month-of-year effects in returns and trading volume
primary_sources.finding: Across seven exchanges and more than fifteen million observations, return anomalies were not persistent across time even though lower weekend trading activity was persistent.

primary_sources.title: The day-of-the-week effect on Bitcoin return and volatility
primary_sources.publisher: Research in International Business and Finance
primary_sources.finding: The 2013-2018 study finds that return effects vary by sample period and associates the reported Monday mean with higher volatility.

independence_and_duplicate_boundary.distinct_from_closed_dra_weekend_veto: The closed DRA calendar family vetoed entries by whether the prior day was Monday-through-Friday. This family has no DRA signal or inventory and owns BTC only during the externally specified UTC Monday interval.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.distinct_from_closed_intraday_session: The closed session family entered every day for an eight-hour activity window. This family uses a weekly twenty-four-hour calendar interval and may not inherit or shift that session result.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.distinct_from_closed_halloween_and_turn_: This rule has no month selection or month-boundary event and cannot be combined with either closed seasonal family.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.prohibited_rescue: Do not inspect or substitute Tuesday through Sunday, a weekday bundle, weekend, local timezone, shifted boundary, partial exposure, short direction, holding extension, price filter or interaction after outcome access.

adversarial_prior: The reported literature effect predates the 2019-2024 repository window and may have disappeared as Bitcoin markets matured.
A mean Monday premium can be driven by a few extreme weeks or by higher volatility rather than repeatable risk-adjusted return.
A weekly round trip incurs enough fee and adverse slippage to consume a small raw calendar effect.
Four years of Design and two years of Validation contain many weekly episodes but only six annual regimes, so annual breadth and concentration are mandatory.
A roughly one-seventh exposure policy can reduce drawdown mechanically; it must exceed time-proportional upside and pass Calmar gates rather than claim value from low exposure alone.
stop_conditions: Freeze one hypothesis, one runner, one manifest and all source, clock, cost, Design, Validation, weekday-spread, path-risk, breadth, concentration and determinism gates before repository weekday outcomes are calculated.
Use only UTC Monday 00:00 through Tuesday 00:00, one full-capital BTC-or-cash variant and zero cash yield.
Stop NO_CANDIDATE on any required gate failure and permanently close the exact family without changing weekday, timezone, boundary, sizing, direction, cost or gate.
Do not open post-2024 outcomes. A historical pass remains REPORTED_NOT_ACTIVATED and requires one separately sealed independent OOS.
missing_proof: No repository 2019-2024 weekday return or strategy outcome has been calculated under this family.
No hash-bound runner or manifest, matched-capital economics, candidate, OOS or forward evidence exists.
